entity_ranked_evidence.title: Venezuela confirms 3 people have died of hantavirus infections, with 2 more deaths suspected - Greenwich Time
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: CARACAS, Venezuela (AP) — Venezuela confirmed on Tuesday that three people died of infections of hantavirus, but stressed there was no evidence of human-to-human transmission in the South American country, which has rarely reported cases of the rodent-borne disease in humans. The Health Ministry said hantavirus was also suspected in the deaths of two health workers in the southwestern state of Barinas. The ministry described the deaths in Anzoátegui and Barinas as isolated incidents that “do not represent a risk to the general community." But it added that health workers would be sent to the affected states to “guarantee the health security of all Venezuelans,” without elaborating. The Venezuelan Medical Federation, a national professional group, said the deaths in Anzoátegui were from the same family in the rural municipality of Miranda in the south of the state.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: 'It eats away at my body': The human cost of S Korea's ultra-convenient overnight deliveries - BBC
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # 'It eats away at my body': The human cost of S Korea's ultra-convenient overnight deliveries. A week before her son died Park Mi-suk asked him to quit his job. For more than a year, the 27-year-old had been working overnight shifts at a warehouse for the country's largest online retailer, Coupang. In that time, Park says, her son lost 15kg and often complained of how tired he was. Jang died in 2020 but six years on, Park is still fighting to end what she believes is the reason for his death: night-time deliveries. But the working conditions for warehouse and delivery workers have been the subject of a growing national debate, with their union claiming that suspected deaths from overwork have continued. The Korean delivery workers' union called for a ban on overnight deliveries in 2025, but the union for Coupang's drivers says nearly all of their members prefer working at night.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Israeli paramedic delivers his own baby in the back of an ambulance - Ynetnews
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: When he realized his wife would not reach the hospital in time, he stopped the ambulance on the way to Hadassah Ein Kerem and helped deliver their seventh child. Last week, while Yitzhak “Izzy” Bendahan and his wife Yael were at their home in Beit Shemesh, Yael, 36, who was in the advanced stages of her seventh pregnancy, began feeling contractions and her water broke. Because of the urgency and the heavy traffic on the way to Jerusalem, the two set out for Hadassah Ein Kerem Hospital in a standby ambulance that Yitzhak kept at home as part of his role with Magen David Adom. “Yael was lying in the back on the ambulance stretcher, and I was driving,” Yitzhak said. But at a certain point, Yael warned him that the birth was progressing, and Yitzhak realized they would not make it to the hospital in time.
